audit_notes: M1–M4 replace illustrative marker positions only. Earlier source measurements and far-edge coordinates are preserved, not overwritten.
New X=157 minus island chef edge X=115 gives 42 inches, consistent with recorded family-room-side aisle.

New lower working edge Y=137 minus island dining edge Y=95 gives 42 inches, versus previous 38-inch clearance to nearest peninsula/cleanup counter. Endpoint equivalence or a nearer projection must be checked before calling this a correction.

Previously captured upper guest-facing straight edge X=190 minus lower working edge X=157 gives 33 inches of projected separation across the bilevel assembly. Jon confirmed that C1–C4 describe the upper outer edge and M1–M4 the lower working edge. This is not a measurement of the lower countertop alone; the separately recorded 25-inch depth is not contradicted by this cross-level subtraction.

The prior design used a calculated existing working edge X=165 and proposed X=170. New capture places the working edge at X=157. A five-inch translation of this newly captured working edge would place it at X=162, whereas rebuilding a confirmed 25-inch-deep row with a proposed far face X=195 would still place the new working edge at X=170. These are different design operations; counter envelope and wall constraints must be reconciled before reusing the concept.
No full wall perimeter, continuous circulation clearance, or service feasibility is established by this capture.

New M5/W1=(138.5,216.5) supersedes the earlier nominal W1 coordinate for future studies. Using old C3=(146,177), their point-to-point distance is about 40.2 inches, which does not reconcile the earlier direct approximately 54-inch tape. Preserve the direct measurement pending physical endpoint verification; do not call either value a verified passage width.

Jon confirmed that C1–C4 are on the outer guest-facing raised countertop edge and M1–M4 on the kitchen-facing lower countertop edge. IMG_8603 shows the two levels and different end projections. Treat the levels as separate outlines; do not add their nominal depths without locating overlap, riser and overhangs.

Jon repeated the C3-to-M5 direct tape as 53.5 inches, corroborating the earlier approximately 54 inches. Preserve 53.5 as the direct point-to-point measurement. Existing C3=(146,177) and latest M5=(138.5,216.5) compute about 40.2 inches and therefore cannot both describe those physical endpoints accurately in the same datum frame. Do not solve for or overwrite a coordinate from the distance alone. This direct diagonal distance does not by itself establish a walkable passage width.

Latest correction: C3=(145,178.5), explicitly remeasured by Jon. M5 X reference confirmed as wall behind range. With M5=(138.5,216.5), coordinate differences are 6.5 inches in X and 38 inches in Y; point distance is about 38.6 inches. Direct 53.5-inch tape remains controlling for point distance. Neither M5 Y nor any other coordinate is mathematically replaced to force agreement.

Jon reconfirmed the measurements after the M5 Y check. Stop repeated coordinate recapture without new diagnostic evidence. The unresolved issue is whether the physical datum planes/lines, endpoint identities and measurement heights represent a single shared horizontal coordinate frame. The schematic map may have contributed endpoint ambiguity. No particular cause is established.

Jon supplied a circled photo identifying C3 and emphasized that the visible tape is broadly consistent with the reported distance, not a 38.6-inch separation. Accept endpoint identification and the 53.5-inch reported direct distance. Exact graduation visibility is not the material issue. Treat the existing coordinate-based passage placement as unresolved rather than repeatedly questioning the direct tape. Preserve all raw readings.

New independent approximate local C3→M5 component offsets are (37,40.5) inches. They imply about 54.9 inches, approximately 1.4 inches longer than direct 53.5. This supports approximate relative placement and indicates that the prior global-coordinate interpretation of X separation (only 6.5 inches, with opposite sign under positive local interpretation) is inconsistent with local field evidence. Exact cause remains undiagnosed; do not average or rescale to close the residual.

Jon reported M5→M6 = 27 inches after defining M6 as the painted-wall/nearest sliding-door-casing seam. This is a directly reported exposed-wall length, not a global X or Y displacement. The photo identifies the wall and openings; their plan angles remain unsurveyed.

Jon reported M5→M7 = 33 inches. Together with M5→M6 = 27 inches, this establishes two adjacent exposed-wall lengths. Wall directions and angles remain unresolved; do not treat either length as a global X/Y displacement.

Jon estimates C3→M6 at approximately 65 inches. It satisfies triangle closure with C3→M5=53.5 and M5→M6=27 (26.5 < 65 < 80.5). This is plausible local geometry, not a new contradiction. Retain estimate status; do not request higher precision merely to draw a rough local boundary diagram.

Jon estimates C3→M7 at 70–71 inches. This range forms feasible triangles with C3→M5=53.5 and M5→M7=33. Together with approximate C3→M6=65 and M5→M6=27, it supports a local relative wall-boundary illustration. Estimated inputs remain estimated and no global datum mismatch is declared resolved.

Jon reports passage-side dining chair width including arms 23.5 inches, projection from tabletop edge to chair back of 19 inches when comfortably occupied, and 36 inches when pulled out enough to stand. Additional pullout projection is 17 inches. Chair position/orientation relative to the local reference has not yet been captured, so no remaining passage width is calculated.

Jon supplied chair-identification photo showing a foreground wooden armchair with striped seat and black back cushion and rounded adjacent tabletop rim. Associate reported 23.5/19/36-inch chair dimensions with this chair. Do not infer operating state or exact table outline from image; retain old table measurements without interpreting their corner definitions anew.

Wide photo resolves spatial chair assignment: the relevant passage is at the French-door-side rounded table end (left in the image). Assistant previously designated the black-cushioned opposite-end chair from a close-up; this was an identification mistake. TC is explicitly redefined at the center of the French-door-side rounded rim before any TC data were captured. Prior chair dimensions remain recorded but are not automatically transferred as verified measurements to the passage-side chair.

Jon reported C3→TC=109 inches following the revised French-door-side rounded-end definition and horizontal measurement request. Keep this as a direct field distance in the normal extended-table configuration. Do not compare it as equivalent to prior guest-edge/table shortest gaps or use it alone to assign a table coordinate.
next_measurements: M5→TC: direct horizontal distance from the same projecting wall corner to the same marked table-rim point TC. Measure from M5 at tabletop height to keep the tape level, using the same vertical wall corner rather than baseboard or trim.

Use this second tie with C3→M5=53.5 and C3→TC=109 to constrain TC locally, selecting the physical branch from identified topology. Table long-axis direction still needs a separate reference before placing its footprint or chair envelopes.
Confirm whether the recorded chair dimensions apply to the passage-side armchair before final occupied/exit clearance calculations.
